## Comparability caveat

All five companies report on a calendar fiscal year (Jan 1 – Dec 31), so there is no fiscal-year mismatch [DOC-1]. However, **Alaska Air Group's FY2024 is not organically comparable to the other four or to its own prior periods**: Alaska closed its acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings on September 18, 2024, and Hawaiian's results are consolidated only from that date forward, contributing $869 million of revenue and a $113 million net loss to Alaska's FY2024 [DOC-2]. Alaska's FY2024 margins therefore blend a full year of legacy Alaska with ~3.5 months of a loss-making acquiree. Excluding the acquired operation, Alaska's revenue base would be roughly $10.9 billion and net income roughly $508 million (a ~4.7% net margin) rather than the reported 3.4% — which would move Alaska ahead of the reported figure but not past United or Delta.

Also note for Southwest that net income ($465M) exceeds operating income ($321M) [DOC-1], so its net margin ranks higher than its operating margin — an ordering shift driven by non-operating items rather than operating performance.

## Operating margin, FY2024 (operating income ÷ total operating revenue)

| Rank | Airline | Operating income | Revenue | Operating margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Delta | $5,995M | $61,643M | 9.7% [DOC-1] |
| 2 | United | $5,096M | $57,063M | 8.9% [DOC-1] |
| 3 | Alaska | $570M | $11,735M | 4.9% [DOC-1] |
| 4 | American | $2,614M | $54,211M | 4.8% [DOC-1] |
| 5 | Southwest | $321M | $27,483M | 1.2% [DOC-1] |

Alaska (4.86%) and American (4.82%) are effectively tied; the ordering is within rounding and is sensitive to the Hawaiian consolidation noted above.

## Net margin, FY2024 (net income ÷ total operating revenue)

| Rank | Airline | Net income | Revenue | Net margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Delta | $3,457M | $61,643M | 5.6% [DOC-1] |
| 2 | United | $3,149M | $57,063M | 5.5% [DOC-1] |
| 3 | Alaska | $395M | $11,735M | 3.4% [DOC-1] |
| 4 | Southwest | $465M | $27,483M | 1.7% [DOC-1] |
| 5 | American | $846M | $54,211M | 1.6% [DOC-1] |

## Conclusion

Yes — Delta Air Lines ranks first on both measures (9.7% operating margin and 5.6% net margin), with United a close second on each [DOC-1]. The only ordering difference between the two rankings is at the bottom: American ranks 4th on operating margin but 5th on net margin, swapping with Southwest.

ANSWER: Operating margin: Delta 9.7% > United 8.9% > Alaska 4.9% > American 4.8% > Southwest 1.2%. Net margin: Delta 5.6% > United 5.5% > Alaska 3.4% > Southwest 1.7% > American 1.6%. Yes — Delta is top-ranked in both (note: Alaska's FY2024 includes Hawaiian only from Sept 18, 2024, so it is not an organically comparable figure).
